mainTopic: The לחמי תודה: the כהן's one-in-ten share, the flour and number of loaves, and how far the comparison to תרומת מעשר goes
overview: The משנה teaches that from each of the four kinds of loaves brought with a קרבן תודה, one whole loaf out of ten goes to the כהן as תרומה. The rest of the loaves are eaten by the owner. A ברייתא learns the amount 'one out of ten' from תרומת מעשר. It first weighs logic against a comparison to ביכורים and then settles it with the shared words 'ממנו תרומה'. The ברייתא then works out the flour: each חמץ loaf takes one עשרון, learned from שתי הלחם, and the מצה matches the חמץ with another ten עשרונות. The מצה comes in three kinds, so there are forty loaves in all, and four of them go to the כהן. The גמרא then examines lines of the ברייתא. It explains 'ממנו' as 'while still together' and shows why the source is תרומת מעשר rather than the תרומה of מדין or תרומת חלה. רבא asks whether a non-כהן who eats this תרומה is punished like one who eats real תרומה, and whether it makes a mixture forbidden; these questions end in תיקו. The amud closes by asking how the word 'תהיינה' teaches its rule, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: one out of ten loaves goes to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: From each kind of loaf of the תודה, one out of ten is taken as תרומה for the כהן. The rules about this come from a פסוק, and the rest of the loaves belong to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: From all the kinds of loaves, he would take one out of ten as תרומה. The פסוק says: 'And he shall offer from it one of every offering as a תרומה to ה׳.' 'One' means a whole loaf, not a sliced piece. 'Of every offering' means every kind of loaf is treated the same, so you may not take from one kind to cover another kind. 'To the כהן who throws the blood of the שלמים it shall belong.' The rest is eaten by the owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states the law: one loaf out of every ten from each kind of תודה bread goes to the כהן. It also shows which words in the פסוק teach the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase in the פסוק teaches a separate rule. The word 'אחד' means a whole loaf. The phrase 'מכל קרבן' means each of the four kinds needs its own תרומה. The end of the פסוק tells us who gets the תרומה (the כהן) and, by implication, who gets the rest (the owner).

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין: our משנה
A portion set aside and given to the כהן
A sliced or broken piece (not a whole loaf)
The כהן who throws the blood of the קרבן on the מזבח
The owners: the person who brought the קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: From each of the four kinds of תודה loaves, one whole loaf out of ten goes to the כהן. Each kind needs its own separate תרומה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the regular תרומה taken from produce. It is a special 'תרומה' taken from the תודה loaves, and it goes to the כהן who did the עבודה with the blood.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
From all of them he would take
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the four kinds of loaves that come with the תודה.

"Of every offering": that all the offerings should be equal,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכּוּלָּם הָיָה נוֹטֵל אֶחָד מֵעֲשָׂרָה תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new משנה about the תרומה taken from the תודה loaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One whole loaf out of ten from each kind of תודה bread goes to the כהן. Each kind is separated on its own, and the rest is eaten by the owner.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains the same פסוק and adds one rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns the rules of the משנה from the same פסוק. It adds one new rule from the word 'ממנו': the loaves must be together when the תרומה is taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And he shall offer from it' means from loaves that are joined together. 'One' means he should not take a sliced piece. 'Of every offering' means all the offerings are equal, so he should not take from one kind of offering for another kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the same פסוק as our משנה. The ברייתא also learns something from the word 'ממנו' ('from it'), which the משנה did not explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new rule is 'מן המחובר': you may take the תרומה only from loaves that are together in one place, not from loaves spread apart. The other two rules, a whole loaf and each kind separately, match the משנה exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: From what is joined together: the loaves must be in one place
Equal: every kind is treated the same way
For its fellow: taking from one kind to cover a different kind

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Rabbis taught: "And he shall offer from it": from what is joined together,
phrases.notes: 'From it' tells us all the loaves have to be together, like one unit, when the תרומה is taken.

phrases.english: "One": that he should not take a sliced piece,
"Of every offering": that all the offerings should be equal,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the round-bracket word; the square-bracket word is the corrected wording. Both mean 'equal.'

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יִטּוֹל מִן הַקׇּרְבָּן עַל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: that he should not take from one offering for another,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that reads the משנה's פסוק and adds one rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תרומה is taken only from loaves that are together. It must be a whole loaf, and each kind is separated on its own.

steps.title: How big is the תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out that the פסוק says 'תרומה' but never says how much it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A תרומה to ה׳': I do not know from how many it is taken.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question: the פסוק calls it 'תרומה', but how many loaves is it taken from? This sets up the next step, where the ברייתא tries to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה simply said 'one out of ten.' But the word 'אחד' in the פסוק only says to take one loaf. It does not say one out of how many. So the ברייתא needs another source for the number ten.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know: the opening of a question
From how many

phrases.english: "A terumah to ה׳":
I do not know from how many it is,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the other words of the פסוק, the ברייתא notices that the amount is missing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the ratio of the תרומה taken from the תודה loaves?

steps.title: Learning 'one out of ten' from תרומת מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The word 'תרומה' appears here and also by תרומת מעשר. Since תרומת מעשר is one out of ten, the תודה loaves are also one out of ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will reason it out. 'תרומה' is said here, and 'תרומה' is said about תרומת מעשר. Just as there it is one out of ten, so here it is one out of ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with a גזרה שוה, a comparison based on the same word. The word 'תרומה' links the תודה loaves to תרומת מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומת מעשר is a tenth of the לוי's מעשר. Because the תורה uses the same word 'תרומה' in both places, the ברייתא moves the 'one out of ten' amount over to the תודה loaves. This gives the משנה a source for its number.

keyTerms.meaning: I will reason it out: the start of a derivation
Learning from a word that appears in two places
The tenth of his מעשר that the לוי gives to the כהן
Just as there, so too here: the standard comparison formula

phrases.english: I will reason it out:
It says here "terumah,"
and it says about terumah of the tithe "terumah,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:26

phrases.english: just as there it is one out of ten,
so too here it is one out of ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵינִי דָּן: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״תְּרוּמָה״, וְנֶאֱמַר בִּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר ״תְּרוּמָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 with a גזרה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shared word 'תרומה' links the loaves to תרומת מעשר, so the amount is one out of ten.

steps.title: A competing comparison to ביכורים, which have no set amount
steps.stepSummary: Maybe we should compare to ביכורים instead, which are also called 'תרומה'. ביכורים have no set amount, so the תודה loaves would have no set amount either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go this way: 'תרומה' is said here, and 'תרומה' is said about ביכורים. Just as there it has no set amount, so here it has no set amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own answer. The word 'תרומה' also appears by ביכורים, which point to a very different result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word-link only works if we know which other place to link to. ביכורים are also called 'תרומה', and ביכורים have no minimum amount. So the comparison from step 4 is now uncertain. The ברייתא will need a reason to choose תרומת מעשר over ביכורים, and steps 6-8 work this out.

keyTerms.meaning: Or go this way: a competing line of reasoning
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
It has no set amount

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer. The ברייתא is testing its own proof. The משנה's ruling of one out of ten still stands, and the ברייתא will go on to explain why תרומת מעשר is the better comparison.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
It says here "terumah,"
and it says about first fruits "terumah,"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:17, where ביכורים are called 'תרומת ידך'.

phrases.english: just as there it has no set amount,
so too here it has no set amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ כְּלָךְ לְדֶרֶךְ זוֹ: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״תְּרוּמָה״, וְנֶאֱמַר בְּבִכּוּרִים ״תְּרוּמָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the גזרה שוה of step 4 by offering a competing one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the תודה loaves to תרומת מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word 'תרומה' also appears by ביכורים, which have no set amount. So the word alone cannot decide which comparison is correct.

steps.title: The תודה loaves are more like תרומת מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא argues that the תודה loaves resemble תרומת מעשר, because neither has another תרומה taken after it, while ביכורים do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which one it is more like. We should learn a תרומה that has no other תרומה after it from another תרומה that has no other תרומה after it. ביכורים cannot be the model, because another תרומה is taken after them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge from ביכורים by showing that the תודה loaves are more similar to תרומת מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the תודה's תרומה is taken, nothing more is separated. The same is true of תרומת מעשר, which is the last gift taken. With ביכורים, the farmer still has to separate תרומה and מעשרות afterward, so ביכורים are a weaker match.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see which one it resembles; the start of a logical comparison
We learn one case from another by logic
No other תרומה is taken after it
It cannot serve as proof or as the model

phrases.english: Let us see which one it resembles:
We learn a תרומה that has no other תרומה after it
from a תרומה that has no other תרומה after it,
and ביכורים cannot serve as the model,
since another תרומה comes after them.
phrases.notes: After the farmer gives ביכורים, he still has to separate תרומה from the rest of his crop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the comparison to תרומת מעשר against the ביכורים challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a closer logical similarity to the original comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the תודה loaves follow ביכורים and have no set amount
steps.terutzMaskana: They are more like תרומת מעשר, since no further תרומה comes after them

steps.title: Or maybe they are more like ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא offers the opposite logic: the תודה loaves and ביכורים are both eaten in a holy place, while תרומת מעשר can be eaten anywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go this way: we should learn a תרומה eaten in a holy place from another תרומה eaten in a holy place. תרומת מעשר cannot be the model, because it may be eaten anywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back with a different similarity that points to ביכורים instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תודה loaves and ביכורים must both be eaten in ירושלים. תרומת מעשר can be eaten anywhere. Now each side has a good similarity, so logic alone cannot decide.

keyTerms.meaning: Or go this way; introduces the opposite line of reasoning
A holy place, meaning ירושלים
Anywhere

phrases.english: Or go this way:
We learn a תרומה that is eaten in a holy place
from a תרומה that is eaten in a holy place,
and תרומת מעשר cannot serve as the model,
since it may be eaten anywhere.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters step 6 with an equally strong similarity to ביכורים
steps.kashyaTarget: The logic of step 6 linking the תודה loaves to תרומת מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Where the תרומה is eaten is also a real similarity, and it points to ביכורים

steps.title: The פסוק decides with a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: Since logic is split, the matching words 'ממנו תרומה' in both places create a גזירה שוה to תרומת מעשר: one out of ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says about the תודה: 'from it a תרומה to ה',' and about תרומת מעשר it says: 'from it a תרומה.' This is for a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא stops arguing from logic and settles the question with matching words in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words 'ממנו תרומה' appear by the תודה and by תרומת מעשר, but not this way by ביכורים. That word link ties the תודה to תרומת מעשר, so its loaves are given at one out of ten.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; a source text settles the question
Learning one law from another through matching words in the תורה
From it a תרומה; the shared words that make the link

steps.whatToRemember: Logic could go either way, so the גזירה שוה of 'ממנו תרומה' decides that the תודה loaves are given at one out of ten, like תרומת מעשר.

phrases.english: The פסוק teaches: 'From it a תרומה to ה','
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:14

phrases.english: and about תרומת מעשר it is written 'from it a תרומה'
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:26

phrases.english: for a גזירה שוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the tie between steps 6 and 7 with a פסוק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תודה loaves are given at one out of ten, learned by גזירה שוה from תרומת מעשר

steps.title: How much flour goes into each loaf?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the amount given to the כהן is known, the ברייתא asks how much flour each loaf needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have learned that the תרומה is one out of ten, but I do not know how much flour each loaf is made from.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes the first question and sets up a new one about the size of each loaf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that one loaf in ten is given does not tell us how big each loaf is. The ברייתא now looks for a source for the flour amount.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned; sums up what was already proven
I do not know; a new question is opened
Here it means a loaf of bread

steps.confusionAlert: Here חלה means a loaf. It is not the מצוה of separating חלה from dough.

phrases.english: We have learned about the תרומה
that it is one out of ten,
but I do not know
how much flour each loaf is made from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion of step 8 and moves to a new question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of flour for each תודה loaf

steps.title: A עשרון per loaf, learned from שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: The word 'לחם' appears by the תודה and by שתי הלחם. Just as each loaf of שתי הלחם is a עשרון, so is each תודה loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: I learn it this way: here it says 'bread,' and there, by שתי הלחם, it says 'bread.' Just as there each loaf is a עשרון, so too here each loaf is a עשרון.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question with another גזירה שוה, this time from the word 'לחם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שתי הלחם brought on שבועות are each made from a עשרון of flour. Because the תורה calls both offerings 'לחם', the תודה's leavened loaves take the same measure.

keyTerms.meaning: I will derive it; introduces the proof
The two loaves offered on שבועות from the new wheat
A tenth of an איפה, a measure of flour
Just as there, so too here; applies the גזירה שוה

steps.whatToRemember: This is the ברייתא's first proposal: one עשרון per loaf, from שתי הלחם. The next steps test it, and the final source turns out to be the extra word 'תביאו' (step 14).

phrases.english: I will derive it:
Here it says 'bread,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:13

phrases.english: and there, by שתי הלחם, it says 'bread.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:17

phrases.english: Just as there it is a עשרון per loaf,
so too here it is a עשרון per loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each leavened תודה loaf takes a עשרון of flour, learned by גזירה שוה from שתי הלחם

steps.title: Maybe the source should be לחם הפנים instead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests another גזירה שוה: 'לחם' also appears by לחם הפנים, where each loaf is two עשרונות. If we learn from there, each תודה loaf would need two עשרונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go a different way: the word 'לחם' is used here, and the word 'לחם' is also used for לחם הפנים. Just as לחם הפנים uses two עשרונות per loaf, so too here, two עשרונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own answer from step 10. It points out that the same word 'לחם' could link the תודה to לחם הפנים instead of to שתי הלחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 used the word 'לחם' to link the תודה to שתי הלחם, which gives one עשרון per loaf. But לחם הפנים is also called 'לחם', and each of its loaves is two עשרונות. So the word alone cannot tell us which source to use.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or go this way' — a phrase that introduces a competing line of reasoning
The showbread: twelve loaves placed on the שולחן in the משכן and בית המקדש
Tenths of an איפה, a measure of flour (singular: עִשָּׂרוֹן)
Learning a law from one place to another because the same word appears in both

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא has dropped its earlier answer. It is testing that answer by showing that the same word could point to a different source.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
"Bread" is stated here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the loaves of the תודה.

phrases.english: and "bread" is stated by the showbread;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:7

phrases.english: just as there it is two tenths,
so too here, two tenths.

steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה from שתי הלחם in step 10
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word 'לחם' also appears by לחם הפנים, which uses two עשרונות per loaf, so the word does not settle which source applies

steps.title: The תודה is more like שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא checks which source is more similar. The תודה and שתי הלחם are both חמץ and both come with an animal offering. לחם הפנים is neither, so it is the weaker comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which one it resembles. We learn a מנחה that comes as חמץ with a זבח from another מנחה that comes as חמץ with a זבח. לחם הפנים cannot serve as proof, because it does not come as חמץ with a זבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to break the tie by asking which source the תודה loaves resemble more. Its first answer points to שתי הלחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תודה loaves include חמץ and are brought along with a זבח, and the same is true of שתי הלחם. לחם הפנים is מצה and comes with no animal offering. By this logic the תודה should follow שתי הלחם, which means one עשרון per loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us see what it resembles' — testing which comparison fits better
'We derive' — we learn the law of one case from another
Leavened bread
An animal offering
'And let it not prove' — that source cannot be used because it is different

phrases.english: Let us see which one it resembles.

steps.title: Logic could also point to לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the opposite comparison. The תודה and לחם הפנים can both come from grain grown in ארץ ישראל or outside it, and from new or old grain. שתי הלחם can come only from new grain from ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go a different way: we learn a מנחה that may come from ארץ ישראל or חוצה לארץ, from חדש or ישן grain, from a מנחה that may come from ארץ ישראל or חוצה לארץ, from חדש or ישן grain. שתי הלחם cannot serve as proof, because they come only from חדש and only from ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on step 12 with a different set of similarities, and these point to לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 compared the offerings by חמץ and by coming with a זבח. Here the comparison is by where the grain may come from and whether it is new or old. On these points the תודה matches לחם הפנים, not שתי הלחם, so the logic is now split evenly again.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside ארץ ישראל
New grain from this year's crop
Old grain from an earlier year's crop
The two loaves brought on שבועות

phrases.english: Or go this way:

phrases.english: we learn a meal offering that may come from the Land or from outside the Land,
phrases.notes: This is the תודה.

phrases.english: from new grain or from old grain,
from a meal offering that may come from the Land or from outside the Land,

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other features (grain from the Land or outside it, new or old grain) match the תודה with לחם הפנים and not with שתי הלחם

steps.title: The extra word 'you shall bring' settles it: one tenth per loaf
steps.stepSummary: Since logic is split, the ברייתא uses the פסוק by שתי הלחם. The extra word 'תביאו' teaches that whatever bread offering is brought 'from another place' follows שתי הלחם. So each תודה loaf is one עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'From your dwellings you shall bring two loaves of waving.' The verse did not need to say 'you shall bring,' so why does it say it? To teach that whatever you bring from another place is like this. Just as there it is a tenth per loaf, so too here, a tenth per loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends the back-and-forth with a פסוק. An extra word in the פסוק of שתי הלחם makes it the model for other bread offerings, including the תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12 and 13 cancelled each other out, so logic alone could not decide. The ברייתא says the word 'תביאו' was not needed, so it must be teaching something. It teaches that other bread offerings follow the pattern of שתי הלחם, which means one עשרון per loaf for the תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches' — introduces a פסוק that settles the question
'From your dwellings'
Bread that is waved — שתי הלחם
'From another place' — any other bread offering
One tenth of an איפה of flour for each loaf

steps.whatToRemember: Each תודה loaf is one עשרון, learned from שתי הלחם. When logic pointed both ways, the extra word 'תביאו' decided the question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic pattern: when two comparisons are equally strong, the ברייתא turns to an extra word in a פסוק to decide.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"From your dwellings you shall bring two loaves of waving";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:17

phrases.english: since there was no need for the verse to say "you shall bring,"
why then does the verse say "you shall bring"?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל מַה שֶּׁאַתָּה מֵבִיא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר
phrases.english: To teach that whatever you bring from another place
phrases.notes: He means any other bread offering, like the תודה.

phrases.english: is like this one.
Just as there it is a tenth per loaf,
so too here, a tenth per loaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״מִמּוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם תָּבִיאּוּ לֶחֶם תְּנוּפָה שְׁתַּיִם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tie between steps 12 and 13 using an extra word in the פסוק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each תודה loaf is one עשרון, learned from שתי הלחם through the extra word 'תביאו'

steps.title: Maybe all the leavened loaves together are only two tenths
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes the comparison to שתי הלחם further. There, the whole offering is only two עשרונות. Maybe the תודה's חמץ loaves together should also be only two עשרונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, just as there it is two tenths, so too here it should be two tenths?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own conclusion from Step 14. If we learn the תודה from שתי הלחם, maybe we should copy its total of two עשרונות, not just its 'one עשרון per loaf'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 used שתי הלחם to teach that each תודה loaf is one עשרון. But שתי הלחם as a whole uses only two עשרונות. So the comparison could be read as 'two עשרונות in total' for all ten חמץ loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: There: the source case we learn from (here, שתי הלחם)
Here: the case we are learning about (the תודה)
A tenth of an איפה, a set measure of flour

phrases.english: But if so: just as there it is two tenths,
phrases.notes: 'There' means שתי הלחם. Its two loaves together use two עשרונות.

phrases.english: so too here, two tenths?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means all ten חמץ loaves of the תודה put together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן שְׁנֵי עֶשְׂרוֹנוֹת, אַף כָּאן שְׁנֵי עֶשְׂרוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the comparison to שתי הלחם from Step 14 should go
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that each תודה loaf is a full עשרון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תודה copies שתי הלחם, perhaps it copies the total amount (two עשרונות) and not the amount per loaf.

steps.title: The word 'תהיינה' shows each loaf is its own tenth
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק by שתי הלחם. The word 'תהיינה' teaches that each loaf is a separate עשרון. So the ten חמץ loaves of the תודה need ten עשרונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'they shall be.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge with one word from the פסוק. That word shows the comparison is about the amount per loaf, not the total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תהיינה' shows that each loaf of שתי הלחם gets its own עשרון. What carries over to the תודה is 'one עשרון per loaf'. Ten חמץ loaves therefore means ten עשרונות.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; it brings a proof from a word in the פסוק
'They shall be', a word from the פסוק about שתי הלחם

phrases.english: The verse says: 'they shall be.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:17. This word teaches that each loaf is its own עשרון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: A word in the פסוק shows which detail is being compared
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ten חמץ loaves together would be only two עשרונות
steps.terutzMaskana: Each חמץ loaf is one עשרון, so there are ten עשרונות
steps.whatToRemember: The ten חמץ loaves of the תודה use ten עשרונות, one for each loaf.

steps.title: Where do we learn ten עשרונות for the מצה?
steps.stepSummary: Now that we know the חמץ needs ten עשרונות, the ברייתא asks where we learn that the מצה also needs ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have learned ten for the חמץ. From where do we know ten for the מצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to a new question about the מצה part of the תודה. This sets up the next step, which gives the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the proofs so far were about the חמץ loaves. Nothing has told us how much flour goes into the מצה loaves. The ברייתא wants a source for that too.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned (it sums up what was already proven)
From where do we know?
Leavened bread
Unleavened bread

phrases.english: We have learned ten [tenths] for the leavened bread;
from where do we know ten for the matza?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמַדְנוּ עֲשָׂרָה לְחָמֵץ, עֲשָׂרָה לְמַצָּה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the finished חמץ amount and asks about the מצה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the מצה loaves also use ten עשרונות

steps.title: The מצה matches the חמץ: twenty עשרונות in all
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings the words 'על חלת לחם חמץ' and learns that the מצה must match the חמץ. So the מצה is also ten עשרונות, and the total is twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'with loaves of leavened bread.' Bring מצה corresponding to the חמץ. So there are twenty עשרונות for the bread of the תודה: ten for the חמץ and ten for the מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by pointing to the פסוק about the חמץ loaves. It learns that the מצה should equal the חמץ, and then adds up the total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק as teaching that the מצה is brought 'corresponding to' (נגד) the חמץ. So the מצה gets the same ten עשרונות as the חמץ. Together that is twenty עשרונות.

keyTerms.meaning: Corresponding to, matching
It comes out that (a tally or result)
The loaves brought with a תודה offering

phrases.english: The verse says: 'with loaves of leavened bread.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:13

phrases.english: Corresponding to the leavened bread, bring matza.
phrases.notes: In other words, the מצה should be the same amount as the חמץ.

phrases.english: So it comes out twenty tenths for the thanks-offering bread,
ten for the leavened bread and ten for the matza.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר עַל חַלֹּת לֶחֶם חָמֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מצה is brought to match the חמץ, so it is also ten עשרונות, for twenty in total
steps.whatToRemember: The תודה uses twenty עשרונות of flour: ten for חמץ and ten for מצה.

steps.title: Maybe all the מצה is one kind
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe all ten עשרונות of מצה are made into just one kind of מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that the ten of מצה should all be of just one kind?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא suggests a wrong idea so that it can reject it. This sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק listing different kinds of מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know how much flour the מצה gets, but not how it is made. Without a source, one could think all the מצה loaves are the same. The word 'יכול' signals a thought that is about to be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (a suggestion that will be rejected)
One kind or type

phrases.english: One might think that the ten [tenths] of matza

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהוּ כּוּלָּן אֶלָּא מִמִּין אֶחָד?
phrases.english: should all be of only one kind?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל עֲשָׂרָה שֶׁבְּמַצָּה לֹא יְהוּ כּוּלָּן אֶלָּא מִמִּין אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the amount of the מצה to the kinds of מצה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether all the מצה is one kind or split into several kinds

steps.title: The פסוק lists three kinds of מצה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes the פסוק of the תודה, which names three kinds of מצה: loaves mixed with oil, thin wafers smeared with oil, and scalded fine flour. So the מצה must be three kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'If he offers it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the thanksgiving sacrifice unleavened loaves mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil, and fine flour scalded…'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the 'one kind' idea by quoting the פסוק. The פסוק itself names three different kinds of מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תורה lists three separate kinds, the מצה cannot all be one kind. The ten עשרונות of מצה are split among these three kinds.

keyTerms.meaning: Thick loaves; here, loaves mixed with oil
Thin wafers smeared with oil
Fine flour scalded in hot water (רבוכה)

phrases.english: The verse says: 'If he offers it for a thanksgiving,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12

phrases.english: then he shall offer with the thanksgiving sacrifice
unleavened loaves mixed with oil,
and unleavened wafers smeared with oil,
fine flour scalded, etc.'
phrases.notes: Count the kinds: loaves mixed with oil, wafers, and scalded flour. That makes three kinds of מצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר אִם עַל תּוֹדָה יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'one kind' idea of Step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק names three kinds of מצה, so the מצה must be split into three kinds

steps.title: The final count: forty loaves, four go to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: Ten עשרונות split among three kinds gives three and a third עשרונות per kind. Each עשרון of מצה makes three loaves, so each kind has ten loaves. With the ten חמץ loaves, that is forty loaves. Four go to the כהן and the owners eat the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: So there are three and a third tenths for each kind, and three loaves per tenth. So the thanks-offering loaves come to forty. He takes four of them and gives them to the כהן, and the rest are eaten by the owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא puts all the pieces together and gives the final numbers. It also says who eats the loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten עשרונות divided by three kinds gives 3⅓ עשרונות per kind. At three loaves per עשרון, each kind has ten loaves, so thirty מצה loaves. Add the ten חמץ loaves (one per עשרון) and the total is forty.

keyTerms.meaning: A third
Priest, who receives part of the offering
The owners who brought the offering

steps.whatToRemember: The תודה has forty loaves in total: ten חמץ and thirty מצה, with ten of each of the three kinds of מצה. Four loaves go to the כהן and the owners eat the rest.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two ratios. The ten חמץ loaves use one עשרון each, but the מצה loaves come three to an עשרון.

phrases.english: So it comes out three and a third tenths
for each and every kind,
and three loaves to each tenth,
phrases.notes: 3⅓ עשרונות times three loaves gives ten loaves of each kind of מצה.

phrases.english: so the thanks-offering loaves come to forty.
phrases.notes: Thirty מצה loaves plus the ten חמץ loaves.

phrases.english: He takes four of them and gives them to the priest,
and the rest are eaten by the owners.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצְאוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה עֶשְׂרוֹנִים וּשְׁלִישׁ לְכׇל מִין וּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the results of Steps 16, 18 and 20 into a final count
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תודה has forty loaves: ten חמץ and thirty מצה in three kinds, made from twenty עשרונות. Four go to the כהן and the owners eat the rest.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the full, practical recipe for the לחמי תודה, and it is the base for the rest of the sugya about these loaves.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא: take the תרומה from loaves that are together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's lesson from the word ממנו: the תרומה must be taken from the loaves while they are joined together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'And he shall present from it' teaches that you take it from what is joined together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא so it can look at it closely. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא read the word ממנו, 'from it,' as meaning 'from it as one group.' So the כהן's loaves are taken while all the loaves are still together, not after they are split up.

keyTerms.meaning: From it
Joined together, kept as one group

phrases.english: The Master said: "And he shall present from it" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:14

phrases.english: from that which is joined together.
phrases.notes: The loaves must still be together in one group when the כהן's share is taken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to a line of the ברייתא to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תרומה of the לחמי תודה is taken from loaves that are joined together, learned from ממנו.

steps.title: The same word ממנו is used for the fats of a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading: ממנו also appears for the fats of the חטאת, and there is no group of separate things to keep together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, it is written 'And all its fat he shall take off from it.' What is there to be joined together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question against the reading of ממנו as 'joined together.' The same word appears with the חטאת, where it seems to mean nothing like that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ממנו always means 'from what is joined,' it should mean that in the חטאת פסוק too. But a חטאת is one animal, so there seem to be no separate pieces to keep together. That makes the ברייתא's reading look weak.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But if so.' This brings a challenge from a rule just stated
Its fat, the parts of the animal burned on the מזבח
He shall lift off, meaning take away

phrases.english: But if so,
that which is written, "And all its fat he shall take off from it" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:19, about a חטאת

phrases.english: there, what joined thing is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading quoted in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading ממנו as 'from what is joined together.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears with the חטאת, where there seems to be nothing that needs to be kept together, so the reading seems not to fit.

steps.title: Remove the אימורין before cutting up the meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב חסדא in the name of אבימי: the meat may not be cut up before the אימורין are taken off. So in the חטאת too, ממנו means taking from the animal while it is still whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: he may not cut up the meat before he takes off the אימורין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. In the חטאת too, ממנו means the animal must still be whole when the fats are removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is something 'joined' in the חטאת after all: the whole animal. The אימורין have to be taken off before the meat is cut into pieces. So ממנו means 'joined together' in both places, and the ברייתא's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He cuts the animal into pieces
The parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח, like the fats

phrases.english: In accordance with what Rav Chisda said that Avimi said,
as Rav Chisda said that Avimi said:
That he may not cut up the meat
before he takes off the sacrificial portions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the word has the same meaning in the second פסוק too
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חטאת has nothing joined, so ממנו cannot mean 'joined together.'
steps.terutzMaskana: In the חטאת, the fats come off while the animal is still whole, so ממנו means 'joined together' there as well.
steps.whatToRemember: ממנו means 'from it while still whole.' The loaves of the תודה stay together until the כהן's share is taken, and the אימורין are removed before the meat is cut up.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא: comparing the תרומה of the תודה to תרומת מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's גזירה שוה: the word תרומה appears by the תודה and by תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: It says 'תרומה' here, and it says 'תרומה' about תרומת מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second line from the ברייתא in order to examine it. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the same word appears in both places, we learn one from the other. תרומת מעשר is one tenth, so the כהן also gets one loaf out of every ten of the תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A portion set aside and given to the כהן
The tenth that a לוי gives to the כהן from his own מעשר
'It says here.' This opens a comparison based on a shared word, a גזירה שוה

phrases.english: The Master said: It is stated here "teruma,"
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the פסוק about the loaves of the תודה.

phrases.english: and it is stated regarding teruma of the tithe "teruma."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to another line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תרומה of the תודה is one out of ten, learned from תרומת מעשר through the shared word תרומה.

steps.title: Why not learn from the תרומה of מדין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we learn from תרומת מעשר and not from the תרומה taken after the war with מדין, which also uses the word תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn it from the תרומה of מדין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison. The word תרומה also appears in another place, and there the amount was not one in ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shared word could link the תודה to more than one place. If we learned from מדין, the amount would come out different, so the גמרא wants to know why תרומת מעשר is the right match.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And let us learn.' This suggests a different source
The share of the spoils of the war with מדין that was given to the כהן and the לויים

phrases.english: But let us derive it from the teruma of Midian?
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:28–30. There the share was a different amount, not one in ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison quoted in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of תרומת מעשר as the source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תרומה of מדין shares the same word, so it could just as easily be the source, and it would give a different amount.

steps.title: Compare something for all generations to something for all generations
steps.stepSummary: The תודה and תרומת מעשר both apply in every generation, so they are compared to each other. The תרומה of מדין happened only once, so it is not used.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn a תרומה that applies in every generation from a תרומה that applies in every generation. The תרומה of מדין cannot prove anything, since it does not apply in every generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we pick the source that is most like the תודה. That source is תרומת מעשר, not מדין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a word could link to two places, we choose the one that is more similar. The תודה and תרומת מעשר both apply in every generation. The תרומה of מדין happened only once, so the one-in-ten rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn one case from another
That applies in every generation
'And let it not prove.' This sets aside a source that does not match

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן's share of the לחמי תודה is one loaf in ten. It is learned from תרומת מעשר because both apply in every generation, unlike the one-time תרומה of מדין.

phrases.english: We derive a teruma that applies for all generations
from a teruma that applies for all generations,
and let the teruma of Midian not serve as proof,
since it does not apply for all generations.
phrases.notes: The war with מדין happened only once, in the מדבר.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין תְּרוּמָה הַנּוֹהֶגֶת לְדוֹרוֹת מִתְּרוּמָה הַנּוֹהֶגֶת לְדוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Chooses the source that is more similar
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תרומה of מדין could be the source for the amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומת מעשר is the better match because, like the תודה, it applies in every generation.

steps.title: Why not learn from תרומת חלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't learn the תרומה of the תודה loaves from תרומת חלה, which is also called תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from תרומת חלה instead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just explained why we learn from תרומת מעשר and not from the תרומה of מדין. Now it raises another possible source: תרומת חלה, which is also called תרומה and also applies in every generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 ruled out the תרומה of מדין because it happened only once. But חלה is given in every generation, just like the תודה and תרומת מעשר. So that reason does not exclude it, and חלה has a different amount (one in twenty-four). The גמרא needs a new reason why it is not the source.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to the כהן, which the תורה also calls a תרומה
And let us learn (it from here)

phrases.english: And let us learn from the תרומה of dough (חלה)!
phrases.notes: The פסוק calls חלה a תרומה too (במדבר 15:20), so it could have been the source for the amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a second competing source after step 27 dismissed the תרומה of מדין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of תרומת מעשר as the source of the גזירה שוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חלה is called תרומה and applies in every generation, so the 'every generation' reason does not rule it out.

steps.title: Only places with 'from it' and 'a תרומה' are compared
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that the comparison works only between places where the פסוק uses both 'ממנו' and 'תרומה'. That leaves out חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: we learn a thing where it says 'from it a תרומה to ה׳' from another thing where it says 'from it a תרומה to ה׳'. This leaves out תרומת חלה, where it does not say 'from it a תרומה to ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל. The link is not just the word תרומה but the full phrase 'ממנו... תרומה', and חלה does not have it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תודה and תרומת מעשר share an extra word, 'ממנו' (from it), next to תרומה. A stronger, fuller match beats a partial one. Since the פסוק by חלה lacks 'ממנו', it is not the source, and the amount stays one in ten.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn (one case from another)
From it, the extra shared word that makes the match
To exclude, to leave out

steps.whatToRemember: The תודה loaves are learned from תרומת מעשר because both פסוקים share 'ממנו' + 'תרומה'. This beats both מדין (a one-time event) and חלה (no 'ממנו').

phrases.english: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
We learn a matter about which it says
"from it, a תרומה of ה׳"
from a matter about which it says "a תרומה to ה׳",
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are ויקרא 7:14 (the תודה) and במדבר 18:26 (תרומת מעשר). Both have 'ממנו' and 'תרומה'.

phrases.english: to leave out the תרומה of dough,
about which it does not say "from it, a תרומה to ה׳".

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual distinction: the link requires the fuller shared phrase 'ממנו' + 'תרומה'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any place called תרומה that applies in every generation, like חלה, could be the source.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only places sharing 'ממנו תרומה' are compared, so the source is תרומת מעשר, not חלה.

steps.title: Is a non-כהן who eats the תודה תרומה punished like with real תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a זר who eats the תרומה of the תודה loaves is liable to מיתה בידי שמים (on purpose) and חומש (by mistake), like with תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: the תרומה of the תודה loaves: is one liable for it to מיתה and חומש, or is one not liable for it to מיתה and חומש?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. Now that we know these loaves are compared to תרומת מעשר, does that comparison also bring the punishments for a non-כהן who eats them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומה, a זר who eats it on purpose is liable to מיתה בידי שמים. One who eats it by mistake pays its value plus an extra fifth (חומש). רבא asks whether these rules also carry over to the תרומה of the תודה loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question he was unsure about)
The loaves brought with the thanks-offering
Death at the hands of Heaven, for a זר who eats תרומה on purpose
An extra fifth paid by a זר who eats תרומה by mistake

phrases.english: רבא asked:
The תרומה of the תודה loaves:
is one liable for them to death and the fifth,
phrases.notes: He means a non-כהן who eats them. On purpose would bring death; by mistake, paying an extra fifth.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶן מִיתָה וָחוֹמֶשׁ?
phrases.english: or is one not liable for them to death and the fifth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the established comparison to תרומת מעשר and asks how far it extends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מיתה and חומש apply to a זר who eats the תרומה of the תודה loaves.

steps.title: The two sides of רבא's question
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains both sides. The comparison to תרומת מעשר may make it exactly like תרומת מעשר, or the words 'בו' and 'חמישיתו' may limit these punishments to real תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is compared to תרומת מעשר, is it like תרומת מעשר? Or perhaps the Merciful One limited it with the words 'by it' and 'its fifth'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא lays out the reasoning on each side of his question. He is not answering it yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On one side, the גזירה שוה ties these loaves to תרומת מעשר, so maybe they share all its rules. On the other side, the פסוקים about death ('ומתו בו', ויקרא 22:9) and the fifth ('חמישיתו', ויקרא 22:14) use limiting words. These may teach that the punishments apply only to real תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was compared (linked through the פסוקים)
It is like, it is treated as
The תורה limited (excluded other cases)

phrases.english: Since it was compared to תרומת מעשר,
is it like תרומת מעשר?
Or perhaps with "by it" and "its fifth"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:9 says 'ומתו בו' and ויקרא 22:14 says 'חמישיתו'. The extra 'it/its' sounds like it means only this case.

phrases.english: the Merciful One limited it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind both sides of the question in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the comparison carry over all rules, or do the limiting words 'בו' and 'חמישיתו' restrict the punishments to real תרומה?

steps.title: Does it make a mixture forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: רבא's second question: if the תרומה of the תודה loaves falls into regular food, does it make the mixture forbidden (מדמעת) like תרומה does?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it make a mixture forbidden, or does it not make a mixture forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a second question based on the same comparison. When this תרומה falls into ordinary food, does the mix become forbidden to non-כהנים, as with regular תרומה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular תרומה that falls into חולין can turn the mixture into מדומע, forbidden to a זר. The question is whether the link to תרומת מעשר covers this rule too, or only the amount to separate.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes a mixture forbidden to non-כהנים (turns it into מדומע)

phrases.english: Does it make a mixture forbidden, or does it not make a mixture forbidden?
phrases.notes: He means when this תרומה falls into regular food. With real תרומה, that mix becomes forbidden to non-כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question from רבא about how far the same comparison reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the תרומה of the תודה loaves creates a forbidden mixture (מדומע).

steps.title: The questions stay unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו. רבא's questions remain unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבא's questions without an answer. They are left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source was found to decide either side. We know only that the amount is learned from תרומת מעשר. Whether the punishments and the mixture rule also carry over stays undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison to תרומת מעשר definitely sets the amount (one in ten). Whether it also brings מיתה, חומש, and מדמעת is left as a תיקו.
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'no'. It means the גמרא could not decide either way.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבא's questions without a resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's questions about מיתה, חומש, and מדמעת for the תרומה of the תודה loaves remain unresolved.

steps.title: How does the word 'They shall be' teach this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's source word ״תהיינה״ and asks how a lesson can be learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said in the ברייתא: the פסוק says "they shall be." What is the lesson learned from this word?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line from the ברייתא and asks how the word ״תהיינה״ proves the ברייתא's point. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used ״תהיינה״ as its source for the flour measure of the תודה loaves, but it never showed how the word teaches this. On its face, "they shall be" says nothing about amounts, so the גמרא asks for the reasoning. The ברייתא's rule is not being challenged here. The גמרא only wants to know how the source works.

keyTerms.meaning: "The פסוק teaches." The words that introduce a proof from a פסוק
"They shall be." The word from the פסוק used as the source
"What is the lesson?" A question asking how a פסוק actually proves the point

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as an attack on the ברייתא. The גמרא accepts the rule and only asks how the word ״תהיינה״ teaches it.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This brings back a line from the ברייתא the גמרא quoted earlier.

phrases.english: The verse states: "They shall be."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:17

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״תִּהְיֶינָה״. מַאי תַּלְמוּדָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's questions end in תיקו (Step 33), the גמרא goes back to analyze another line of the earlier ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word ״תהיינה״ teaches the ברייתא's rule about the flour measure of the תודה loaves.
